source.title: Using Statistics to Automate Stochastic Optimization
source.authors: Hunter Lang; Lin Xiao; Pengchuan Zhang

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendices; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports optimizer comparisons and training/test performance, but does not test the listed claims about memorization, width, architecture, batch-size generalization gaps, dropout, sharpness, or memorized-example removal. It tests a learning-rate scheduling method and stationary statistics instead.
record.gate_note: Optimizer performance and training loss are reported, but no result measures the claim versions' specified generalization gaps or properties. Mentions of other work, including Wilson et al. (2017), are cited prior findings and are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study directly compares Adam with momentum SGD using held-out image-classification accuracy and language-model validation perplexity under limited optimizer tuning. These results bear on V4 even though the paper's main contribution is SASA.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors conclude that SASA competes with the best hand-tuned momentum-SGD schedules, approaches validation-tuned SGD and Adam performance, and improves scheduling robustness through statistical testing. SASA still requires an initial learning rate and drop factor.
record.recipe_differences: The study proposes and evaluates an adaptive learning-rate scheduling method; it does not reproduce the claim versions' interventions or measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors report that noise level and testing frequency affect robustness of the deterministic ratio test relative to SASA; changes to SASA's δ and γ alter drop timing, while ζ does not affect final performance when the learning rate reaches the same level.

fits_no_version.finding: SASA matches tuned SGD schedules and improves robustness to noise and testing frequency relative to a deterministic stationarity test.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Statistical stationarity tests can automate learning-rate drops while preserving competitive predictive performance.

fits_no_version.finding: On MNIST logistic regression, learning-rate-tuned Adam and SASA achieve similar performance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adam and automatically scheduled momentum SGD can perform similarly on regularized convex classification.

record.problems: The study's performance comparisons rely on selected tasks and tuned baselines; authors note that SASA's stationary condition may not exist generally and that their method did not detect overfitting in the COCO experiment.
record.rows_left_out: No qualifying rows: reported outcomes concern the SASA scheduling method or its stationarity tests, not a named claim version. Comparisons such as SASA versus SGM/Adam are outside the catalog claim's measured effects.

untested.parts: Broader hyperparameter tuning, decoupled weight decay, and switching from Adam to SGD. The warmup intervention switches in the opposite direction. Equal or better Adam training performance is not established by the readable text.
Large-batch held-out performance penalties under fixed epoch budgets; the small-batch experiments concern scheduling robustness.
Dropout interventions; the RNN uses fixed dropout.

missing.locator: Section 4, CIFAR-10; Figure 2 top row; Appendix A.1.

missing.what: Adam versus momentum SGD held-out accuracy comparison on ImageNet. Record the explicitly stated Adam deficit and the learning-rate and warmup tuning.
missing.locator: Section 4, ImageNet; Figure 2 middle row; Appendix A.2.

missing.what: Adam versus momentum SGD validation-perplexity comparison on WikiText-2. Both have validation-tuned learning rates and factor-four drops when validation loss stops improving. The supplied figure text does not establish their relative final perplexities, so no directional verdict is justified.

record.verdict_notes: The record incorrectly excludes direct Adam-versus-SGD comparisons as outside the catalog. V4 concerns held-out performance and does not require an explicitly calculated train/test gap. Its rows_left_out explanation therefore needs correction. SASA-only comparisons do not independently establish V4, and unreadable plot values should not be invented.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out natural-label performance under the same recipes.
Width sweep beyond interpolation and test-error behavior.
Convolutional versus fully connected comparisons and local connectivity.
Adaptive versus non-adaptive optimizers under the version's held-out-performance comparisons and tuning conditions.
Large- versus small-batch held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets.
Dropout's effect on held-out error across the stated regimes.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with the train/test gap.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring the resulting test-accuracy change.

relationships.condition: ResNet18 on CIFAR-10 with augmentation, weight decay 0.0005, and batch size 128.
relationships.reason: Section 4 explicitly reports that Adam falls short of tuned momentum SGD in test accuracy despite learning-rate tuning and a tuned 50-epoch SGD warmup. Based on text; the record omitted the comparison.
relationships.display_finding: Adam reportedly achieved lower test accuracy than tuned momentum SGD despite learning-rate tuning and SGD warmup, but the comparison remains unverified.

relationships.condition: ResNet18 on ImageNet with augmentation, weight decay 0.0001, and batch size 256.
relationships.reason: Section 4 explicitly reports worse generalization for Adam than momentum SGD despite tuning and a 30-epoch SGD warmup. Based on text; the record omitted the comparison.
relationships.display_finding: Adam reportedly generalized worse than momentum SGD despite tuning and SGD warmup, but the comparison remains unverified.
